short: Judaea's second great revolt against Rome ended in near-total depopulation of the province.
full:
In 132 CE, Simon bar Kokhba led a Judaean uprising against Hadrian's rule, provoked by a ban on circumcision and plans to build a Roman colony and temple to Jupiter on the site of Jerusalem. Guerrilla tactics and a network of underground hideouts allowed the rebels to seize Jerusalem and control much of Judaea for over two years, minting their own coinage and briefly restoring an independent Jewish state.

Hadrian committed as many as twelve legions under the general Sextus Julius Severus, who ground down the revolt through attrition rather than pitched battle. The rebel stronghold of Betar fell in 135, and Bar Kokhba was killed. Roman sources claim roughly half a million Judaeans died; Hadrian renamed the province Syria Palaestina and barred Jews from Jerusalem, accelerating the diaspora and shifting the centre of Jewish religious life to Galilee and Babylonia.
